issues: Key is documented (listener rules to different target groups; hourly charge per ALB). Decidable without prices. Wrong B/C/D all fail cleanly.

Key is documented: the ELB FAQ states NLB cross-zone enabled incurs regional data transfer between AZs, and the ELB page says disabled nodes use only targets in their own AZ. Equal targets per zone are stated, so disabling is safe; availability requirement holds.
Conceptual overlap with -005 (ALB) and -011 (GWLB) is by design as the NLB/ALB/GWLB cross-zone trio; keep this one as the anchor (difficulty 3, the only one with an availability constraint).

Wrong option A why says 'Cross-zone load balancing is always on for Application Load Balancers'. The ELB docs say it is always enabled at the load balancer level but CAN be disabled at the target group level, so the claim is imprecise (the FAQ says 'always on' while the User Guide page allows target-group disabling: a documented contradiction, add to content/contradictions.json if not present).
The decisive fact for A is that AWS does not charge for ALB regional cross-zone transfer, so disabling saves nothing; word it that way.
suggestedFix: Reword wrong A why: 'AWS does not charge for the regional data transfer caused by cross-zone load balancing on an Application Load Balancer, so disabling it saves nothing on the bill.' Keep the elb-faqs quote ('you are not charged for this type of regional data transfer').
